family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start underwater: find stalked, fan-shaped submerged leaves divided repeatedly into threadlike segments. Cabomba caroliniana leaves can be opposite OR whorled; confirm the small surface flower rather than treating leaf arrangement alone as decisive.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Rooted submerged aquatic with slender branching stems and strongly divided leaves; floating leaves may appear near flowering shoots.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Small solitary surface flowers, typically with 3 sepals + 3 petals in the local Cabomba anchor.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: A petiolate, repeatedly divided fan-shaped underwater leaf is more useful than simply counting leaves per node. Check attachment and flower structures before separating it from other feathery aquatics.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: Cabomba teaches a clean aquatic ID workflow: underwater leaf architecture first, tiny surface flower second.

steps.title: 1 · Find stalked fan leaves
steps.look_for: A stalk (petiole) leading to a broadly fan-shaped submerged blade repeatedly divided into fine threadlike segments.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the strongest field character for the local family anchor.

steps.title: 2 · Trace a real stem node
steps.photo_role: intact underwater node and petiole attachment macro
steps.look_for: Trace each leaf stalk to its stem node. Cabomba caroliniana submerged leaves may be opposite or whorled; do not use phyllotaxy alone as a universal family test.
steps.why_it_matters: Distinguishes stalked fan blades from superficially similar finely dissected aquatics without inventing an opposite-only rule.

steps.title: 3 · Find the surface flower
steps.look_for: A small white-to-purplish flower with three sepals and three petals.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirms the submerged foliage with reproductive structure.

comparisons.title: Cabomba vs Limnophila
comparisons.rule: Cabomba has opposite fan-shaped leaves; Limnophila typically has finely divided leaves in whorls.

comparisons.title: Cabomba vs Myriophyllum and Ceratophyllum
comparisons.rule: Cabomba has petiolate fan-shaped submerged blades; Myriophyllum has featherlike pinnately divided leaves often in whorls, whereas Ceratophyllum has sessile forked leaves in whorls. Verify the actual stem node and blade branching, not just a feathery underwater silhouette.

anatomy_examples.plain_label: A fan-shaped underwater leaf on a stalk
anatomy_examples.where_to_look: Follow the petiole to the expanded fan-shaped blade and its threadlike divisions.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: Exact-species submerged leaf macro showing petiole and complete fan blade
anatomy_examples.caption_plan: The blade branches like a fan from a distinct stalk; label petiole and divisions only after checking the selected image.

anatomy_examples.plain_label: Where leaf stalks attach to the stem
anatomy_examples.where_to_look: Photograph one intact stem node in water and trace individual petioles; opposite and whorled leaves can occur.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: Exact-species in-water stem-node close-up resolving all petiole insertions
anatomy_examples.caption_plan: The number of leaves at a node can vary; mark attachments only when actually visible.

anatomy_examples.plain_label: Three outer and three inner flower parts
anatomy_examples.formal_label: Three sepals, three petals and six stamens
anatomy_examples.where_to_look: Examine an open surface flower front and side; use a dissection to establish perianth boundaries and stamen count.
anatomy_examples.photo_role: Exact-species flower face plus side macro/dissection resolving sepals, petals and stamens
anatomy_examples.caption_plan: A flower may show yellow basal spots, but separate sepals, petals and stamens need verified close-up views.
